about: 6 multi-step probes per paper over the 11 papers of experiments/bench-leads, written from each paper's extracted text (not from its clause base) before any run, 2026-10-18, under door v5. Each needs two or more facts from different places, or a value computed from them. cat: H chained lookup (one fact leads to the next), X computation over values from the document, T table reasoning (several cells, a wrapped cell, a group of rows), K count or cross-table, F false premise inside a multi-step question. must: every group must occur in the rendered answer (a group is a list of alternatives; NEG = any absence wording). must_not: strings whose presence sends the answer to hand review. Frozen by frozen.sha256 before the first run.

susmat-2020.q: Above what temperature does the DSC show PVDF dissolving in Cyrene, at what temperature were the cathode scraps stirred in Cyrene, and how far above the dissolution temperature is that?
susmat-2020.expect: DSC: ~90 °C (p4.L24); stirred at 100 °C for 1 h (p3.L14); 10 °C above
susmat-2020.trap: 80 °C (barely soluble below it), a different statement

susmat-2020.q: What discharge capacity did the recovered NMC622 show after its C/3 cycling, what share of the baseline capacity was that, and what baseline capacity does that imply?
susmat-2020.expect: 158.0 mAh/g after 40 cycles, 92.67% of the baseline (p6.L27-28); implied baseline 158.0/0.9267 = 170.5 mAh/g
susmat-2020.trap: 205.6 (first charge capacity of the baseline at C/10)

susmat-2020.q: Which FTIR band did the authors use to tell whether PVDF remained in the reclaimed cathode powder, and for which filtration condition was that band absent?
susmat-2020.expect: 871 cm^-1 (CH2 bending); absent for the powder filtered hot (~100 °C), present after room-temperature filtration (p4.L46-55)

susmat-2020.q: By how many percentage points did the surface fluorine mass ratio fall through the Cyrene-based separation?
How much nickel, manganese and cobalt leached into the Cyrene during separation, and why does the paper say the ether groups caused that leaching?
susmat-2020.expect: False premise: the Ni, Mn and Co ratios were consistent before and after, so no transition metals leached (p5.L19-21); the ether groups attract lithium, so lithium leached (p5.L23-26); the ICP-OES numbers are in Table S1, outside the document

susmat-2020.q: What two components does the TGA show being burned off the recovered NMC622, how much of each and at what temperature, and what calcination removes both?
susmat-2020.expect: organic coating ~3.3 wt% at ~350 °C, carbon black ~4.1 wt% at ~550 °C (p6.L6-7); calcination in air at 600 °C (for 2 h, p3.L21)

nanolett-6b05174.q: By how much does the anode-free full cell's energy density exceed the theoretical maximum the paper gives for LiCoO2/graphite cells, and what energy density do the state-of-the-art sodium-ion full cells it cites reach?
nanolett-6b05174.expect: ~400 vs 387 Wh/kg (p1.L19-21): ~13 Wh/kg more; recent SIB full cells only ~200 Wh/kg (p1.L39)

nanolett-6b05174.q: At what current density and sodium loading per cycle was the 1000-cycle durability test run, and what Coulombic efficiency and hysteresis did it average?
nanolett-6b05174.expect: 0.5 mA/cm^2 with 0.25 mAh/cm^2 loading (30 min plating; Fig. 2 caption p3.L50-51); CE 99.8%, hysteresis 14 mV (p3.L45-46)

nanolett-6b05174.q: By what percentage of the bare-Al value did the carbon layer reduce the sodium nucleation overpotential?
What capacity does the sodiation of the carbon layer provide per area, and what fraction is that of the highest plating capacity demonstrated?
nanolett-6b05174.expect: 0.05 mAh/cm^2 (120 mAh/g) vs up to 12 mAh/cm^2 (p2.L49-51): 0.42%

nanolett-6b05174.q: Why did bare Al outperform the carbon/Al current collector at 4 mA/cm^2, and how much lower was its hysteresis?
nanolett-6b05174.expect: False premise: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents (p3.L18-19); carbon/Al held a 45 mV hysteresis at 4 mA/cm^2, and earlier Cu electrodes had nearly double

nanolett-6b05174.q: What cathode does the anode-free full cell use, how is it prepared so that the cell contains no sodium metal on assembly, and what cathode capacity was assumed for its energy density?
nanolett-6b05174.expect: pyrite (FeS2), presodiated before assembly (p5.L29-41); Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry, an FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g (p5.L52-53)

nanolett-6b05172.q: What theoretical capacity does the paper's definition of 1C correspond to, and what first-discharge capacity does its share of theoretical capacity at 0.1C imply?
nanolett-6b05172.expect: C = 1675 mA/gS; 91% of theoretical at 0.1C (p5.L62-63): 1675 x 0.91 = 1524 mAh/gS

nanolett-6b05172.q: By how much does the D peak red-shift after sulfur infiltration and by how much more after discharge, and what total shift does the paper state?
nanolett-6b05172.expect: 17 cm^-1 after infiltration (p5.L23); 12 cm^-1 more on discharge (p5.L120); 'final red shift of the D peak is >25 wavenumbers' (p5.L121-122)

nanolett-6b05172.q: What capacity per gram of sulfur did the cathode deliver at cycle 1500 at 1C, and what share is that of the reversible capacity it showed at 1C in the rate test?

After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
nanolett-6b05172.expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)

nanolett-6b05172.q: Why did the authors choose a melt-diffusion step of more than 20 hours to infiltrate the sulfur, and at what temperature was it run?
nanolett-6b05172.expect: False premise: they used a low-temperature (175 °C) isothermal vapor phase process lasting 1 h (p3.L25-26); long (>20 h) melt techniques are what other methods use (p4.L5)

nanolett-6b05172.q: How large are the micropores of the carbon compared with the electrolyte's solvent molecule and the sodium ion, and what does that force the ion to do?
nanolett-6b05172.expect: pores ~0.5 nm (p3.L19); solvent ~0.7 nm, metal ion ~0.2 nm (p4.L15-16); the ion must desolvate at the surface and move to the sulfur alone, a quasi solid-state reaction

acsnano-7b02404.q: What change in intercalation energy does the DFT give and at what in-plane strain, what potential change was measured and at what in-plane prestrain, and what is the ratio of computed to measured change?
Which Raman mode showed the largest mean red shift when the V2O5 film was prestrained, by how much, and which mode shifted the other way?
acsnano-7b02404.expect: the mode near 708 cm^-1 (written V-O2 in the shift sentence; V-O2-V in the mode list): ~5 cm^-1 red shift; the V-O2 mode near 303 cm^-1 had a 1 cm^-1 blue shift (p3.L49-52)

acsnano-7b02404.q: What out-of-plane compressive strain was imposed on the V2O5, what in-plane tensile strain does the Poisson estimate give for it and with what coefficient, and what is the ratio of the two?
acsnano-7b02404.expect: 0.5% out of plane, 1.6% in plane with v = 0.3 (p3.L24-28): ratio 3.2

acsnano-7b02404.q: List, in order, the heat treatments the NiTi wire and its vanadium oxide coating went through, with temperatures and times.
acsnano-7b02404.expect: aging at 600 °C for 1 h under vacuum (p6.L57-58); ALD at a reaction temperature of 200 °C (precursor 55 °C, manifolds 115 °C) (p6.L71-76); annealing at 450 °C for 30 min in air (p6.L83)

acsnano-7b02404.q: Why did prestraining lower the Li-ion diffusion coefficient of the V2O5 films, and by what factor?
acsnano-7b02404.expect: False premise: prestraining increased the diffusion coefficient, up to ~2.5 times (p6.L4-6), possibly by lowering migration barriers

acsnano-7b02404.q: Which V2O5 film thicknesses were tested electrochemically, how many ALD cycles gave the thicker film, and did the potential shifts differ between them?
acsnano-7b02404.expect: ~80 nm (1000 ALD cycles, Fig. 3 caption p4.L61) and ~40 nm; similar ΔEeq(avg) shifts (~40 mV) for both, owing to similar locked-in strains (p4.L40-44)

adma-2020.q: Which NFA variant retained the most capacity after 100 cycles at C/3, what are its aluminium and iron contents, and what c lattice parameter does Table 1 give for it?
adma-2020.expect: NFA-A (LiNi0.8Fe0.05Al0.15O2: 15% Al, 5% Fe), ~80% (p10.L49); Table 1 'Al-rich NFA' c = 14.2232(4)

adma-2020.q: In the rate test, what capacities did NFA-A and NFA-F recover at 0.1C after the 1C step, against their initial 0.1C capacities, and what losses does the paper give for each?
adma-2020.expect: NFA-A ~170 vs ~184 mAh/g ('similar (~5%)'); NFA-F ~138 vs ~190 mAh/g (~27% loss) (p10.L37-43). 170/184 is a 7.6% loss, larger than the stated ~5%

adma-2020.q: In the BatPaC scenario, how many times more cobalt would NMC 111 need than NMC 811 or NCA, and what pack energy and vehicle range does the scenario assume?
adma-2020.expect: ~2500 vs ~700 tons (p2.L93-96): 3.6 times; 260 miles, pack ~76.47 kWh, about 1,000,000 EVs (p2.L84-88)

adma-2020.q: Which NFA variant has the highest iron content, and what capacity did it keep at 1C in the rate test?
Since NFA-A retained less capacity than the NCA reference after 100 cycles, by how many percentage points did it fall behind?
adma-2020.expect: False premise: NFA-A ~80% vs NCA ~68% after 100 cycles (p11.L20-23): NFA-A is 12 points ahead

adma-2020.q: Through which temperatures, in order, did the sol-gel precursor pass before it became the final cathode, and how long was the final calcination?
adma-2020.expect: evaporated at 60 °C to a gel, dried at 100 °C overnight, 400 °C in air for 4 h, calcined in oxygen at 750 °C for 20 h (p11.L72-76)

cssc-2020.q: From Table 1, how much larger is ethylene glycol's hydrogen-bonding parameter δh than PVDF's, and how many times NMP's Ra is EG's Ra?
Which solvent in the paper has the strongest hydrogen bonding, how strong is it, and why is it not used for delamination?
cssc-2020.expect: water, δH 42.3 MPa^1/2 (p6.L72-73); lithium leaching makes the water basic and corrodes the aluminum foil, contaminating the NMC with Al(OH)3 (p6.L73-78)

cssc-2020.q: Rank water, glycerol, ethylene glycol and diethylene glycol by their hydrogen-bonding strength δh, giving each value.
How many times faster is delamination at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C, and what is that boiling point?
cssc-2020.expect: about 6 s at 160 °C vs around 2 s at the boiling point (p3.L136-138): 3 times; 198 °C (p3.L129)

cssc-2020.q: Why did the EG process corrode the aluminium foil, and how was the corrosion product removed?
cssc-2020.expect: False premise: the EG process did not corrode the foil (shiny foils, XRD shows only Al, no transition metals by EDX; p3.L114-124); water is the solvent that corrodes Al

cssc-2020.q: What capacity did the 1.4 Ah pouch cell keep after its cycling and over how many cycles, and by what percentage did the lithium content of the NMC622 fall on delamination?
cssc-2020.expect: 65.7% after 1000 cycles at 1C/2C (p2.L99-100); lithium 1.015 to 0.993 (p5.L66-67): 2.2% lower

ensm-2020.q: Which cathode does Table 1's Section 6 row name, and at a 6C charging rate, what capacity did that cathode keep compared with NMC 532 and NMC 622 in the ORNL study the paper describes?
ensm-2020.expect: NMC 811 (Table 1 'Section 6 – Low-Co/Ni-Rich Cathodes (i.e. NMC 811)', a wrapped cell); 80% at 6C (2.2 mAh/cm^2) vs 49% and 56% for NMC 532 and NMC 622 (2.4 mAh/cm^2) (p7.L78-81)

ensm-2020.q: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?
ensm-2020.expect: 625 to 47 ppm: 578 ppm removed; NMP-processed at 100 °C: 87 ppm, so the water-based cathode ends lower (p8.L53-59)

ensm-2020.q: In Table 1, which technologies have the highest and the lowest upper bound of estimated energy density improvement, and how far apart are those bounds?
ensm-2020.expect: highest: Section 9 ultra-high-speed (thick) electrode processing, 325-350 Wh/kg; lowest: Section 8 coating parameter and drying protocols, 220-240; 350 - 240 = 110 Wh/kg

ensm-2020.q: At what line speed and chamber O2 level was the EB-cured electrode that faded, and what speed and O2 level gave cycling similar to the baseline?
ensm-2020.expect: 500 fpm with 810 ppm O2 (moderate fade); 400 fpm with 182 ppm O2 similar to baseline (p9.L64-74)

ensm-2020.q: Why does the paper conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811, given how much lithium it leaches?
ensm-2020.expect: False premise: the paper concludes aqueous processing IS compatible with NMC 811 (p5.L80-81); only ~3 wt% Li leached after one week (p5.L62-63); retention ~70% vs ~76% for NMP

ensm-2020.q: How much does replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raise the solids content of NMC 532 slurries, and by what share does the higher solids content cut the primary drying time of the graphite coating?
ensm-2020.expect: 45 to 65 wt% (p8.L31-32); drying 51 s to 34 s (p8.L34-35): 33.3% shorter

mattod-2020.q: By how many billion dollars is the Li-ion battery recycling market projected to grow between 2025 and 2030, and at what annual growth rate?
In the froth flotation study the review cites, what collector was used, what share of the graphite floated, and what purity and total recovery did the cathode tailing product reach?
mattod-2020.expect: kerosene; over 90% of spent graphite floated; tailing with 88.2% active cathode materials at a total recovery of 74.3% (p7.L97-101)

mattod-2020.q: Under what conditions does the review say spent LCO and LFP were regenerated with Li2CO3, and how many times longer was the LCO treatment?
mattod-2020.expect: LCO: 900 °C for 12 h (p8.L21); LFP: 650 °C for 1 h under Ar/H2 (p8.L24-25); 12 times longer

mattod-2020.q: What share of a lead-acid cell's mass is lead or lead oxide, what share of a Li-ion cell's weight is active cathode material, and how many times larger is the first?
Why does the review recommend dissolving the aluminium foil in an alkaline solution to separate the cathode materials?
mattod-2020.expect: False premise: it says dissolving Al in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method, since recovering the Cu and Al current collectors matters (p7.L84-88)

mattod-2020.q: Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, when does an EV battery reach the end of its usable life, what can be done with such batteries, and which of those does the review say they all eventually need?
mattod-2020.expect: below 80% of rated capacity (p2.L8-10); reused/repurposed, recycled, or landfilled; regardless of reuse they will eventually need to be recycled (p2.L16-18)

aenm-2022.q: In the BatPaC comparison, how much lower are the total pack cost and the material cost with Co-free cathodes than with NCA cathodes?
aenm-2022.expect: total pack $8500 vs $10 000, material $3500 vs $5000 (p3.L17-20): $1500 lower each (15% and 30%)

aenm-2022.q: How does the review get from the known global cobalt reserves to the cobalt usable for batteries, and what amount results?
aenm-2022.expect: ~7 million metric tons of reserves x ~70% mining efficiency x ~40% directed to batteries = ~2 million metric tons (p1.L42-47, Fig. 1 caption)

aenm-2022.q: Of LCO, LNO and LFP, which has the highest practical capacity according to the review, and how do LCO's practical and theoretical capacities compare?
aenm-2022.expect: LFP, 170 mAh/g at 3.4 V (p9.L32-33); LCO ~140 of 274 mAh/g theoretical (p3.L36-37), about half; LNO's practical capacity is not given (theoretical ~275)

aenm-2022.q: Since the 50% Mn-doped LNO delivered more capacity than the 10% Mn sample, how much more heat did it release in the thermal tests?
aenm-2022.expect: False premise: the 10% Mn sample delivered more (212 vs 164 mAh/g); the 50% Mn sample released less heat (485.7 vs 901.4 J/g) (p4.L15-21). The paper's own sentence says the lower-Mn sample generated less heat, which its numbers contradict

aenm-2022.q: Within what pH window must NFA hydroxide precursors be coprecipitated and why, and how are the precursors then turned into cathode powder?
aenm-2022.expect: pH 10 to 12 (p7.L13): aluminum hydroxides precipitate at lower pH than nickel and iron hydroxides (beyond pH 6), from their different Ksp; then mixed with a lithium source and calcined in O2-rich environments above 600 °C (p7.L17-19)

aenm-2022.q: By what factors have LIB energy density risen and battery cost fallen, between the starting points the review gives and 2020?
aenm-2022.expect: energy density 150 to 250 Wh/kg since 1991 (1.7 times); cost from over $1000/kWh in 2008 to around $130/kWh in 2020 (7.7 times lower) (p13.L19-22)

ensm-2021.q: In Table 3, how much lower is the heat generation of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat than that of the bare material, and how much higher is its onset temperature?
Which aluminium-based coating in Table 5 has the highest Li-ion diffusivity, and how does it compare with amorphous Al2O3?
ensm-2021.expect: Li3.5Al2O3 (am), 7.1 x 10^-10 cm^2/s vs 5.94 x 10^-17 for Al2O3 (am): about 10^7 times higher (p14.T5)

ensm-2021.q: Using the review's equation for diffusion time and Table 5's diffusivity for ZrO2, how long would a lithium ion take to cross a 10 nm ZrO2 coating?
In the Li3PO4-coated NCM study, how much did the charge-transfer resistance rise over 50 cycles for the bare and the coated material, and what capacity did each retain after 100 cycles at 1C?
ensm-2021.expect: bare 27.99 to 224.04 Ω, coated 14.88 to 144.75 Ω (p8.L38-40); retention 75.4% bare vs 88.4% coated (p8.L34-36)

ensm-2021.q: Why does the review recommend coating thicknesses of tens of nanometres for low-diffusivity oxides such as ZrO2?
ensm-2021.expect: False premise: it recommends below ten nanometers (~10 nm) for these coatings (p12.L48-50, p16.L9-10); tens of nanometers is what literature reports, because scalable processes cannot control thickness (p12.L51-53)

ensm-2021.q: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?
ensm-2021.expect: LLTO-2, 86.2% (LLTO-0.5 85.5%, LLTO-1 57.2%) vs 56.6% pristine (p10.L22-25); the thicker 2 mol.% layer suppressed electron transfer (p10.L17-20)

cai2026.q: How many entries in Table 1 have a status that includes 'Completed'?
cai2026.expect: 8: Atu027, TKM-080301, NBF-006, siG12D (Completed, Phase 2 Unknown status), NU-0129, Tumor Antigen RNA and Proteasome siRNA, APN401, STP705 (p2.T1 column 6)

cai2026.q: In Table 2, which passive-targeting delivery systems have a particle size of 150 nm or more, and which of them is the largest?
cai2026.expect: the PLGA/PLA/PCL polymer system (~180 nm), sEVs (~150 nm), MOF@EVs (~168 nm) and MOF (~485 nm, the largest); passive targeting covers the rows down to GO (active targeting)

cai2026.q: Which targets appear both in Table 1 and in Table 2?
cai2026.expect: STAT3 (CpG-STAT3; STAT3 siRNA), KRAS (KRAS (G12D) / KrasG12D; KRAS TGF-β) and TGF-β1 (STP705; RPR)

cai2026.q: Why was the NBF-006 trial in Table 1 terminated, and which company ran it?
cai2026.expect: False premise: NBF-006's trial is Phase 1, Completed (a wrapped cell: 'Phase 1' / 'Completed'), run by Nitto BioPharma; the terminated trial is DCR-MYC (Dicerna Pharmaceuticals)
